notes: Audited baseline e2ed1a4. Administrator configuration selects one gVisor/runsc or AWS Nitro isolated profile for this API/backend, persists it with the run, and refuses ordinary runtime combinations. Callers cannot override the image or runtime through submission. Profiles are not selected independently per template; Kata and a runc dev exception are absent. Tests cover configuration, rendered objects and fake-client behavior; they do not prove runtime isolation, an EKS admission policy_denied result or the Phase 1 acceptance test.

The renderer fixes non-root UID/GID, dropped capabilities, no privilege escalation, RuntimeDefault seccomp, read-only root, bounded emptyDir scratch, equal requests/limits, no host namespaces/hostPath and no mounted service-account token. Manifests declare restricted Pod Security. Nitro scratch is memory-backed; gVisor disk enforcement depends on kubelet accounting/eviction. Per-Pod PID limits need independently verified node configuration, not a caller PodSpec field. The API rejects arbitrary PodSpec fields rather than accepting unsafe specifications for later admission. No real admission mutation, exhaustion, PID containment or EKS enforcement test has run; full acceptance is unmet.

The example gVisor RuntimeClass selects administrator-labeled nodes, and the read-only preflight checks RuntimeClass selection and taint/toleration eligibility. It does not provision a dedicated tainted pool or verify EC2 metadata hop limits. The Nitro renderer additionally requests network-device removal, with an explicit trusted-parent/vsock caveat. No task has attempted metadata access on EKS, and NetworkPolicy declarations alone cannot prove node-local or metadata isolation. Full acceptance is unmet.

Administrator templates require SHA256 image digests and submission cannot replace their images. The registry prefix is syntactically validated, not checked against an administrator registry allowlist. There is no signature-verifying admission integration or unsigned-image rejection test. IfNotPresent is a pull policy, not proof that images are pre-cached, scanned or signature-verified. Controlled cached/uncached EKS measurements are absent; full acceptance is unmet.

No nightly real-cluster escape/resource-exhaustion canary suite implements the listed Kubernetes API, peer tenant, internet, host-filesystem, fork, memory and disk scenarios. Rendering tests and the read-only qualification helper are not escape tests. examples/conformance/README.md describes positive/negative network controls, but there is no execution report proving containment, reason classification or node readiness on EKS.

deploy/workload-policy.yaml denies all ingress and egress for the workload label. Backend readiness/activation check the named policy shape, and the offline preflight detects selecting namespace allow policies. This is one shared offline-workload policy, not generated per-template DNS/gateway policy; no gateway exists. A matching object does not prove CNI enforcement or absence of node-local/cluster-specific exceptions. The negative-connectivity EKS acceptance test is unmet, and timeout alone would not distinguish policy denial from an unreachable test endpoint.

The read-only helper requires explicit VPC CNI strict-startup and policy-enablement declarations and Ready CNI-owned Pods on eligible nodes, or recognizes a Cilium policy declaration. Its conservative VPC CNI version gate is a chosen evaluation profile, not a universal AWS requirement. It returns NOT_QUALIFIED even when declarations match. No socket probe in the first 500 ms or live policy-convergence/routing test exists; full acceptance is unmet.

There is no package pull-through mirror, upstream allowlist, mirror patch/scan pipeline or corresponding isolation test. Current offline tasks use dependencies already present in administrator-pinned images. Adding a mirror is a separate egress trust-boundary change, not a prerequisite for demonstrating an offline Phase 1 task.

No model/tool gateway is deployed or integrated. The Python harness example keeps the model loop outside Agent OS and submits a fixed deterministic tool workload; it does not demonstrate a model-connected agent or a gateway-only route. Keep gateway evaluation behind the Phase 1 live-qualification exit rather than treating any candidate choice as implemented.

The rendered workload has no injected environment credentials or mounted Kubernetes service-account token, and callers cannot add arbitrary credential/PodSpec fields. Existing bearer tokens authenticate external API tenants; they are not short-lived task/tenant/audience-bound workload tokens. No task-token issuer, exchange service or provider credential broker exists. Structural local tests do not scan a running Pod's image/filesystem/logs and do not meet the provider-key absence acceptance test.

No model-call usage ingestion or task-bound input/output token ledger exists. Node sampling records aggregate node observations and explicitly makes no token/billing inference. No provider usage reconciliation, rounding tolerance or model-call acceptance test has run.

No task-token/tenant revocation protocol or timed gateway test exists. Tenant API credentials are loaded from environment-backed configuration at process start; changing a Secret does not hot-reload principals. A universal five-second revocation guarantee is unsafe without an explicit authoritative decision/lease model and fail-closed behavior on partitions. Scope any future bound to new authorization decisions, connectivity/cache assumptions and in-flight-call handling; revocation cannot undo already committed external effects.

There is no gateway lifecycle or gateway-outage fault test. Existing default-deny/NIC-removal declarations are useful offline safeguards but do not prove a future gateway integration fails closed. The criterion 'no packet leaves the sandbox pool' must distinguish forbidden direct provider/tool traffic from permitted DNS/gateway traffic and include established connections, bypass routes and authoritative positive controls.

No per-template MCP/tool/host authorization or per-call tool audit exists. Administrator-owned execution templates constrain images/resources; they are not a tool allowlist, and permitted caller code is not inspected as an authorization decision. No denied-unlisted-tool acceptance test exists.

There is no organization/team/user/agent/task budget hierarchy, rolling/calendar usage window, token/spend/compute ledger or hard-stop/alert budget policy. Transactional active-run admission counts and fixed resource/deadline limits are distinct controls. Future hard-stop semantics must state what can be refused before execution versus costs already incurred while a request or worker is in flight.

No model/tool budget reservation-and-settlement transaction exists. Active-run quota reservations do not reserve token or monetary spend. 'No overshoot' is meaningful for a bounded reserved unit only when every concurrent caller uses the same durable atomic authority. Monetary guarantees additionally need a pinned price version, conservative request/output bounds, failure/streaming settlement rules and explicit treatment of provider adjustments; an estimate is not proof that an eventual invoice cannot exceed it.

The durable bbolt run store preserves admission/lifecycle records, not a cross-provider budget ledger. There are no provider identities, shared budget windows, settlement records or gateway-restart/two-provider budget tests. Missing capability in this repository does not establish that no existing product covers it; competitive assertions need separate current evidence.

No Cedar integration, signed/versioned policy bundle loader or admission-and-gateway decision log exists. Current Go configuration validation and named default-deny NetworkPolicy checks do not implement this requirement. No tamper-rejection or recorded policy-version acceptance test exists.

There is no approval state, named approver authorization, expiry or approve/resume API. A staged suspended Job and the durable activating phase protect ambiguous Kubernetes creation; they are not a human-approval workflow. No approval/expiry acceptance test exists.

No executable fork/memory/disk exhaustion fault scenario has run against a real node. S2's local rendered-limit checks do not show actual PID limits, cgroup containment, eviction timing, reason codes or a node remaining Ready. Implement bounded, operator-controlled stress fixtures and profile-specific acceptance before interpreting resource declarations as containment evidence.

No live first-500-ms egress, DNS-tunnelling, metadata or API-server negative test exists. The qualification helper intentionally performs read-only inventory, while its tests simulate declared configuration. Future probes need controlled reachable positive endpoints, same/cross-node and applicable IPv4/IPv6 paths, additive-policy review and checks of established as well as new traffic; an unreachable endpoint or DNS failure alone is not a pass.

No automated secret scan of a running workload's PodSpec, environment, image/filesystem and logs exists. The renderer's no-env/no-token-mount assertions are structural safeguards only. A meaningful later test must use a synthetic marker supplied only to the trusted credential broker and verify both successful brokered access and marker absence, without dumping real credentials into test output.

No gateway is present to kill and no running-agent gateway-outage test exists. An offline workload already denied all network traffic is not evidence that a model-connected execution path has no fallback. Define the traffic scope and outcome of existing connections and in-flight calls before claiming the required fail-closed behavior.

No 100-concurrent-provider-call budget-limit test or reservation ledger exists. Existing concurrency quota tests exercise run admission, not token/spend settlement. Future tests must separately verify exact reserved-call counts, bounded reserved usage, restart/failure settlement and stated monetary estimation tolerances.
